TEACHE VALLEY GENERAL HOSPITAL -- EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT DISCHARGE SUMMARY Name: Leonard Fontenot MRN: LGH-6043-2217 DOB: 1/19/27 Age: 34 Arrival: 10/19/2061 Discharge: 10/19/2061 ED attending: Dr. Ngozi Eberhardt
Dictating now for the discharge summary of Mr. Fontenot. This is a thirty-four-year-old right-handed man who presented to the emergency department on the nineteenth of October with five days of worsening facial pressure, thick green nasal drainage, a headache behind the eyes and a low-grade fever that he measured at one hundred point four. He says he had a cold that began around the first of October and got better and then got much worse, the classic double worsening. He has had sinus trouble on and off since the previous winter. He was last treated with Augmentin in January 2058 and finished the course.
The social history is long and I will give it as I have it. He lives with his wife Delphine and their two children Remy, who is nine, and Odile, who is six, in a rented duplex at 118 Coulee Rouge Lane in Lafayette, owned by Mr. Gaspard Hebert. His father Armand, ninety-one, lives on the other side of the duplex, and he is the primary caregiver for him. Delphine's grandfather Emile Guidry, age 94, is at a nursing home in Opelousas. Their neighbor, Mrs. Thibodeaux, helps with the children. Patient is under a great deal of stress and reports hearing gunshots in the neighborhood several nights a month which is keeping him awake.
Exam showed temperature 37.9, heart rate 96, blood pressure 124 over 80, tenderness over both maxillary sinuses and erythema of the nasal turbinates. Impression was acute bacterial sinusitis. He was discharged on amoxicillin clavulanate for ten days, saline irrigation, and told to return for any vision change or swelling around the eye. ENT follow up if not better. Phone (337) 555-0183, wife 337-555-0107.
Dictated by Ngozi Eberhardt, MD, 10/19/2061 22:41. Dictated but not read. Please excuse any transcription errors
